question: What is a model trained on these auto-labels worth, against the same model trained on human labels of the same images?
why: Precision against a finite-category reference is a bound: an unmatched box is either a real object VisDrone omits or a false positive, and no further verifier distinguishes them. A downstream model does not need to. A real-but-unannotated box raises its score and a false box lowers it, so training prices exactly the population the reference cannot adjudicate. The published auto-labelling claim this tests is that auto-labels reach 90-95% of human-label downstream performance, and that downstream performance peaks at moderate verifier thresholds rather than high ones.

labelling_configuration.note: the recommended configuration, unchanged; stricter verifier thresholds are applied afterwards to the recorded verifier score, so one labelling pass serves every threshold arm

train_slice.selection_rule: stems of train.txt whose VisDrone sequence prefix (before the first underscore) does not occur in val.txt, sorted, then random.Random(11).sample(pool, 200), sorted
train_slice.leakage_rule: sequence-level exclusion against val: frames of one sequence are near duplicates, so a shared sequence would put val content in training under both arms and flatter the auto arm by the same amount it flatters the human arm, which is still a false comparison

evaluation.reported_as: the auto arm as a fraction of the human arm

class_mapping.rule: the dataset's own three-class convention, verified box-for-box against labels/{split} on 60 sampled images before any arm was built
class_mapping.dropped_meaning: ignored regions, bicycle, tricycle, awning-tricycle, motor and others are unlabelled in this layout, so they are background for the human arm too
class_mapping.ontology_dropped_reason: emitting a class the human arm leaves as background would penalise the auto arm for labelling what the reference declines to label, which measures the convention and not the labels

parent_fallback_policies.why: conservative naming emits the parent `vehicle` on 64.7% of matched boxes on the held-out panel, and `vehicle` has no single counterpart among car and longvehicle. How that fallback is resolved is therefore a declared label policy and not an implementation detail.
parent_fallback_policies.drop: boxes labelled `vehicle` are omitted, so only exactly-named boxes train
parent_fallback_policies.verifier_label: a `vehicle` box takes the verifier's own label where that label maps, and is omitted otherwise; this is the parent-refinement measurement that was flagged as the obvious next step and is priced here rather than asserted
parent_fallback_policies.modal: every `vehicle` box becomes `car`, the modal class, which is the prior a labeller with no further evidence would use
parent_fallback_policies.retrieval: a `vehicle` box takes the class its nearest neighbours carry in a bank of human-labelled reference crops from the training split, excluding every sequence the labelled images belong to; added after the panel naming table showed retrieval resolves 0.547 of fallbacks into usable consumer classes against the verifier's 0.357 at 0.135 wrong against 0.036, which a naming table cannot adjudicate because a wrong child label and an absent one cost a consumer differently

arms.labels: the dataset's own human labels for the same 200 images

student.identical_across_arms: images, image count, architecture, weights, hyperparameters, seed and the val split; only the training labels differ
student.additional_seeds_rule: further seeds are added to every arm or to none, so a seed is never spent on the arm that happens to be ahead

limits: the student is scored against the same three-class human labels, so it measures consumer utility under VisDrone's conventions and not truth; a real object this dataset never labels still counts against the arm that labels it
200 images and one architecture is a direction, not a gate, and VisDrone remains outside assumption A4

ultralytics has no ignore-region support, so a region this pipeline records as unsearched or unresolved trains as background; the export writes those regions to a sidecar and the count is reported rather than hidden
COCO-pretrained initialisation means both arms start from a model that has seen external data; the comparison between arms is unaffected because it is identical for both

amendments.not_part_of_the_frozen_protocol: the threshold ladder and the three original fallback policies were declared before any label existed; this arm was declared after seeing the panel naming table and before any student was trained on it, and is reported as the later addition it is
